title: requests, REST APIs, retry, rate limiting
exp:
Fetching from REST APIs with proper error handling is core to the 50-source S&P pipeline.

Understanding requests, REST APIs, retry, rate limiting at a senior engineering level requires inspecting the runtime execution context, internal memory allocations, and network/storage constraints. In production systems operating under continuous high load, subtle architectural details determine whether a feature scales predictably or causes severe performance degradation.
pts: requests.get(url, params={}, headers={}, timeout=10) -- timeout is mandatory without exception.
response.raise_for_status() -- raises HTTPError for 4xx/5xx. Call after every request.
requests.Session() -- reuses TCP connection; persists headers and auth across calls.
Pagination: loop until next_page is None or results are empty.
code:
import requests, time, os
from requests.adapters import HTTPAdapter
from urllib3.util.retry import Retry

session = requests.Session()
session.headers.update({'Authorization': f'Bearer {os.environ["API_KEY"]}'})
retry = Retry(total=3, backoff_factor=1, status_forcelist=[429,500,502,503,504])
session.mount('https://', HTTPAdapter(max_retries=retry))

def fetch_all(base_url: str) -> list:
    records, page = [], 1
    while True:
        resp = session.get(f'{base_url}?page={page}&per_page=100', timeout=10)
        resp.raise_for_status()
        data = resp.json()
        records.extend(data.get('items', []))
        if not data.get('next_page'): break
        page += 1
        time.sleep(0.5)   # respect rate limits
    return records

qa.q: Why is timeout mandatory in every requests.get()?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Without a timeout, requests.get() waits forever if the server hangs. In a pipeline running at 2am, a hung call blocks indefinitely with no error. Always set timeout=10 to get a requests.exceptions.Timeout you can catch and handle.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Python interpreter executes bytecode under the CPython Global Interpreter Lock (GIL), managing objects via reference counting and cycle GC.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Attempting CPU-bound parallelism with Python threading fails due to GIL serialization; memory leaks occur from circular references.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Multiprocessing bypasses the GIL for CPU tasks at the cost of inter-process communication (IPC) serialization overhead.

qa.q: How do you distinguish transient from permanent API failures?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Transient: 429 (rate limit), 500-504 (server temporarily unavailable), Timeout -- worth retrying. Permanent: 404 (not found), 400 (bad request), 403 (auth failure) -- retrying won't fix these; skip, fix, or escalate.
